serviceDesk.title: Service Desk
serviceDesk.subtitle: Email-intake ticketing with stakeholder turnaround tracking

dashboard.matrixTitle: Open tickets by stakeholder and age
dashboard.empty: No open tickets. New email requests will appear here automatically.

detail.detectedIssuesHint: The first issue stays on this ticket. Select any remaining issue that should become its own ticket.
detail.splitFailed: The issues could not be split. No partial tickets were created.
detail.saveFailed: Those changes could not be saved.
detail.emailStakeholderHint: Sent from the desk's watched mailbox, so the reply comes back to this ticket. Only addresses configured in Master Data for this ticket's stakeholders, and the requester, can be chosen.

ai.title: AI email categorisation
ai.description: Let AI read incoming emails and suggest the Request Type and Product. When off, ticket owners classify tickets manually.

autoSplit.title: Automatic ticket split
autoSplit.description: When AI reads an email and finds exactly two clearly different requests, and is confident about both, log the second one as its own ticket. Everything else stays a single ticket flagged for triage, so a person decides.
autoSplit.requiresAi: Turn on AI email categorisation first. Nothing is split without it.

manual.title: Log a ticket
manual.subtitle: For a request received by phone or WhatsApp
manual.subject: Subject

templates.title: Email templates
templates.description: Edit the copy for the automated emails. Use the placeholder tokens listed under each template.
templates.subject: Subject

varDesc.requester_name: The sender's name from the incoming email.
varDesc.display_id: The ticket id with your workspace prefix, e.g. TKT-000123.
varDesc.subject: The subject line of the incoming email.
varDesc.desk_name: How the desk signs its mail — your workspace name, unless overridden in desk settings.
varDesc.additional_tickets: Filled only when one email was split into more than one ticket; empty otherwise.
varDesc.closure_note: The resolution summary written when the ticket was resolved.
varDesc.overall_days: Total working days the ticket was open.
varDesc.scope: Which slice of tickets this digest covers (e.g. one department); empty for the whole desk.
varDesc.total_open: Count of open tickets in the digest.
varDesc.breaching: Count of tickets past the red threshold.
varDesc.tickets_block: The generated list of open tickets — keep this in the body.
varDesc.date: The date the digest was generated.
varDesc.breach_days: Your workspace's red threshold, in working days.

settings.mailboxesHint: Every email sent to a registered mailbox becomes a ticket. The channel is how that mail reaches Aexy.
settings.channelWebhookHint: Your email provider (Postmark, SES, SendGrid or Mailgun) pushes mail to Aexy's inbound email webhook. Nothing arrives until the provider is pointed at it — this is for addresses whose mail is already routed through one of those providers.
settings.channelGmailHint: Aexy reads this inbox through a connected Google account. Add is refused unless that exact address is connected — so pick one below, or connect it here.
settings.name: Name
settings.readOnly: You have read-only access to Master Data. Ask a workspace admin or service desk manager to make changes.
settings.masterDataHint: The three tables the desk sorts incoming email against. The sender's domain decides which account a ticket belongs to and who it lands on — mail that matches nothing goes to triage.
settings.accountsHint: Who the desk works for. When mail arrives, its sender domain is looked up here: the ticket is attributed to that account and assigned to the owner set below. A whole email address can be used instead of a domain, and beats a domain entry — use one when several accounts share a provider like gmail.com.
settings.accountsEmpty: No accounts yet, so every incoming email lands in triage and is given an arbitrary owner. Add the domains you receive requests from and tickets start routing themselves.
settings.vendorsHint: Outside parties the desk sends work to. Mail from these domains is read as a vendor replying about existing work rather than a customer raising something new. It still goes to triage — a vendor is not an account.
settings.vendorsEmpty: No vendors yet. Mail from anyone who is not a known account is treated as an unknown sender.
settings.productsHint: What a ticket can be about. AI categorisation picks one by exact name and the daily digest groups by it, so a name the AI suggests that is not listed here is dropped.
settings.productsEmpty: No products yet, so tickets are not tagged with one and the digest cannot group by it.

serviceDesk.noDepartment: You're not in a department yet, so no tickets can be routed to you. Ask an admin to add you from Organization → Departments.
serviceDesk.assignedOnly: You see the tickets assigned to you, and none are open right now. Other tickets on the desk are handled by their own owners.

workingHours.title: Working hours
workingHours.description: The breach clock only runs during these hours, IST. It stops overnight, at weekends, and on company holidays — so "2 business days" means two of these shifts, not 48 hours. Holidays come from the Leave module.
workingHours.summary: Shift is {hours}h, so the 2-day target is twice that.
workingHours.invalid: The end must be later than the start

deskIdentity.title: Desk identity & targets
deskIdentity.description: Ticket id prefix, the timezone day boundaries resolve in, and the breach thresholds. These were fixed in code; the values shown are the defaults still in force if you never change them.
deskIdentity.prefixInvalid: 1–10 letters or digits, starting with a letter.
deskIdentity.thresholdsInvalid: Amber must be a smaller number of days than red, and both above zero.
deskIdentity.prefixWarning: Saving relabels every existing ticket as {prefix}-1234. Replies quoting the old prefix will still thread correctly.

deskDepartment.title: Ticket intake
deskDepartment.description: Which department receives incoming tickets. Its members are auto-assigned new requests, and its head gets the digest of everything still open.
deskDepartment.nobody: No department is receiving tickets, so every request arrives unassigned and nobody gets the digest. Choose one, or give a department the function your first queue routes to.
deskDepartment.noneExist: This workspace has no departments yet, so there is nothing to route tickets to. Create one under Organization → Departments, then choose it here.

testSla.title: Temporary minute SLA test
testSla.description: Tickets normally turn amber and red after whole working days, so verifying breach colours, escalations, or the digest would mean waiting days. This compresses time for a controlled test: each ticked stage's SLA becomes the working-minute thresholds you enter — for every ticket in the workspace — until the expiry, when it stops on its own. End test removes it immediately.
testSla.example: Example: tick one stage with amber 2 and red 5, send a test email in, and its ticket turns amber after 2 working minutes and red after 5. Unticked stages keep the real SLA, and breach reporting is real while the test runs — everyone in the workspace sees the test colours.
testSla.invalid: Tick at least one stage, use a future expiry within 24 hours, and give every ticked stage a red value greater than its amber.
testSla.active: Test mode is active. It is ignored automatically after its expiry.
